plan: This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the clock exit price determines rank order, and the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of how the clock proceeds. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Since my value is $25, I should bid exactly $25 to ensure I win whenever profitable and never overpay relative to my valuation.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my own bid only determines when I exit, not what I pay if I win. Therefore, bidding my true value ($31) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.

Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. My value is $9, so I will bid exactly $9.
